title: Fewer Keys on the Ring
story:
NORA: GATEKEEPER CAPABILITY COUNT 14
NORA: GATEKEEPER REQUIRED CAPABILITIES 1
NORA: AUDITOR WREN FLAGGED EXCESS PRIVILEGE

The `gatekeeper` container serves the crew login page on port 8150 and runs with Docker's default bundle of 14 Linux capabilities. Its only privileged act is binding to port 80 inside the container.

Wren's note, pinned beside the alert: "Least privilege is not a suggestion. Take every key off the ring, then hand back the one it needs." Recreate `gatekeeper` that way.
objectives: Replace container `gatekeeper` with one from `python:3.12-alpine`, publishing host port 8150 to container port 80
Run `python -m http.server 80 --directory /gate` with `/workspace/gate` mounted read-only at `/gate`
Drop ALL capabilities and add back only `NET_BIND_SERVICE`
The login page at http://localhost:8150 must still load
startingState: Container `gatekeeper` is running with the default capability set; the login page lives in `/workspace/gate/`.
hints: Linux splits root's powers into separate capabilities, and Docker gives each container a default set of 14. You can remove capabilities when creating a container, and add specific ones back. Binding a port below 1024 is one such capability.

`--cap-drop ALL` removes the whole default set, and `--cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE` returns the single one the web server needs. The order of the flags does not matter, but the container has to be recreated.

```bash
docker rm -f gatekeeper
docker run -d --name gatekeeper \
  --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE \
  -p 8150:80 -v /workspace/gate:/gate:ro \
  python:3.12-alpine python -m http.server 80 --directory /gate
docker inspect -f '{{.HostConfig.CapAdd}}' gatekeeper
```

commands: docker run -d --name gatekeeper -p 8150:80 -v /workspace/gate:/gate:ro python:3.12-alpine python -m http.server 80 --directory /gate

validation.description: All default capabilities are dropped (`CapDrop` contains ALL)
The main process holds only the bind-service capability
The crew login page still loads on port 8150

solution: docker run -d --name gatekeeper --cap-drop ALL --cap-add NET_BIND_SERVICE -p 8150:80 -v /workspace/gate:/gate:ro python:3.12-alpine python -m http.server 80 --directory /gate
debrief: Capabilities slice root into small privileges, and dropping ALL then adding back one by name is the strictest form of least privilege Docker offers. Pro tip: if a dropped container fails, its error message names what is missing, so add capabilities back one at a time rather than reaching for `--privileged`.
